Programs recognize software providers and sourcing partnerships driving business and IT transformation

LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Information Services Group (ISG) (Nasdaq: III), a global AI-centered technology research and advisory firm, has announced the winners of the 2026 ISG Software Innovation Awards™ and the ISG Paragon Awards™ for Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA).

The winners of both programs were recognized at the 2026 ISG Sourcing Industry Awards gala dinner on Tuesday, November 17, at Fairmont Windsor Park. The ISG Software Innovation Awards celebrate software providers whose innovations drive business and IT transformation, and the ISG Paragon Awards recognize the use of new approaches and technologies in sourcing industry partnerships.

“Congratulations to the EMEA winners of the 2026 ISG Software Innovation Awards and ISG Paragon Awards, who are setting new standards for innovation and enterprise transformation,” said John Boccuzzi, Jr., partner and president, ISG Research. “Their achievements show how advances in technology, exceptional service delivery and strong client-provider partnerships can create measurable, lasting business value.”

ISG Software Research analysts selected the following winners of the 2026 ISG Software Innovation Awards for EMEA:

Overall Software Innovation: The digital innovation that most successfully maximizes the value of people, processes, information and technology

  • Winner: Xactly for Xactly Intelligence

Artificial Intelligence Award: The software provider that best exemplifies innovation in technologies supporting analytics, data intelligence, data platforms, generative AI, governance, machine learning and AI, operations and streaming and events

  • Winner: Publicis Sapient for Bohdi

Business and Technologies Award: The software provider that best exemplifies innovation in technologies supporting customers and CX, digital business and workplace, employees and HCM, office of finance and accounting, office of revenue and supply chain and operations

  • Winner: Infosys for CPS.ai

Industries Award: The software provider that best exemplifies innovation in technologies supporting automotive, CPG & retail, energy, financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, public sector, media & telecom or travel & hospitality

  • Winner: Aspire Systems for AFTA 5.0

Information Technology Award: The software provider that best exemplifies innovation in technologies supporting ADM & DevOps, cloud & infrastructure, compute, edge, network & IoT, cybersecurity, intelligent automation, IT management & operations, observability and platforms

  • Winner: ABBYY for Document AI

The 2026 ISG Paragon Awards introduce a new methodology that recognizes up to five winner subcategories within each award category.

Providers are expanding their work across intelligent workflows and business outcomes, as enterprises seek greater innovation, broader service scope and increased output from provider partnerships. The updated methodology recognizes partnerships for distinct contributions to innovation, impact, performance and culture. It also recognizes individuals and small teams for exceptional ownership, expertise or initiative. All winner subcategories carry equal standing.

An independent, expert panel of judges selected the following winners of the 2026 ISG Paragon Awards for EMEA:

AI Pacesetter: Substantial business impact through the adoption of AI

  • Paragon Challenger — Bold Innovation and Change: LTM and a global enterprise
  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: Infosys and Microsoft Corporation
  • Paragon Contender — Consistent High Performance: Infosys and bp

Excellence: Outstanding delivery by a service provider

  • Paragon Challenger — Bold Innovation and Change: UST and FrauDfense
  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: Techwave and Eurochange (Western Union)
  • Paragon Commendation — Excellence in Values and Culture: Wipro and ABB
  • Paragon Contender — Consistent High Performance: Stefanini and Evonik

Innovation: Imagination and entrepreneurial spirit in helping organizations future-proof their businesses and better serve clients

  • Paragon Challenger — Bold Innovation and Change: Ramco Systems and Etihad Airways Engineering
  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: EvoluteIQ and The AA
  • Paragon Commendation — Excellence in Values and Culture: UST and Aviva Investors
  • Paragon Contender — Consistent High Performance: DATAGROUP and EEW Energy from Waste GmbH

Partnership of the Year: A high-performing partnership that drove exceptional business outcomes

  • Paragon Challenger — Bold Innovation and Change: Infosys and Telenet
  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: Publicis Sapient and RWE
  • Paragon Commendation — Excellence in Values and Culture: Orion Innovation and Liverpool Football Club
  • Paragon Contender — Consistent High Performance: HCLTech and E.ON Group
  • Paragon Standout — Exceptional Collaboration and Shared Success: LTM and SCANIA AB

Sustainability: Implementations that delivered measurable environmental and/or social outcomes for clients, consumers, communities and/or employees

  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: Wipro and Novartis Foundation
  • Paragon Commendation — Excellence in Values and Culture: ATELIWARE SOFTWARE LTDA and SISTECH

Transformation: The successful transformation of an organization or key business function

  • Paragon Challenger — Bold Innovation and Change: Infosys and NatWest
  • Paragon Champion — Outstanding Business Impact: Mphasis and APTIA
  • Paragon Commendation — Excellence in Values and Culture: Cognizant and The Football Association
  • Paragon Contender — Consistent High Performance: ITC Infotech and British American Tobacco

The November 17 gala dinner also recognized winners of the ISG Provider Lens™ Awards, honoring outstanding performances by providers featured in ISG Provider Lens studies, and the ISG Star of Excellence™ awards, which recognize excellence in provider delivery based on enterprise client feedback. Full details are available on the award website.

About ISG

ISG (Nasdaq: III) is a global AI-centered technology research and advisory firm. A trusted partner to more than 900 clients, including 75 of the world’s top 100 enterprises, ISG is a long-time leader in technology and business services that is now at the forefront of leveraging AI to help organizations achieve operational excellence and faster growth. The firm, founded in 2006, is known for its proprietary market data and research, in-depth knowledge and governance of provider ecosystems, and the expertise of its 1,500 professionals worldwide working together to help clients maximize the value of their technology investments.

Key Terms

generative aitechnical
Generative AI is a type of computer technology that can create new content, like text, images, or music, on its own. It’s important because it can produce realistic and useful material quickly, which could change how we create art, write stories, or even develop new products. Think of it as a smart robot that can invent and produce things almost like a human.
machine learningtechnical
Machine learning is a set of computer programs that learn patterns from large amounts of data and improve their predictions or decisions over time, like a recipe that gets better each time it’s adjusted based on taste tests. For investors it matters because these systems can speed up analysis, spot trends or risks humans might miss, automate routine work, and potentially create competitive advantages or cost savings that affect a company’s performance.

iottechnical
The Internet of Things (IoT) describes a network of everyday devices—such as appliances, vehicles, and equipment—that are connected to the internet and can share data automatically. For investors, IoT represents a growing trend that can drive efficiency and innovation across many industries, potentially creating new opportunities for growth and value. Its expansion influences how companies operate and compete in a digitally connected world.

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vizsla Silver Corp. (TSX: VZLA) (NYSE: VZLA) (Frankfurt: 0G3) ("Vizsla Silver" or the "Company") is providing an update on the continued advancement of its wholly owned Panuco silver-gold project ("Panuco" or the "Project") in Mexico. 

Vizsla Silver continues to advance key development activities at Panuco with a focus on construction readiness. M3 Engineering & Technology has now completed approximately 50% of engineering and approximately 85% of the process plant equipment currently contemplated for the Project has been ordered. As previously disclosed, three key development contracts for the Project have been awarded, including engineering procurement and construction management (EPCM), mine design and equipment supply (see press releases dated April 23, 2026 and June 16, 2026, respectively), with the main mining contract to be awarded in due course. In parallel, the Company continues to work closely with Mexican federal authorities to strengthen security arrangements in preparation for a phased return to site.

"We have made significant progress advancing Panuco this year, achieving important milestones in engineering, procurement and development planning," said Michael Konnert, President and Chief Executive Officer. "We are well positioned to  move into the next phase of development, with safety guiding our preparations for a phased return to site and first silver production now anticipated in the second half of 2028."

"This progress has come during an exceptionally difficult year, and we have remained focused on supporting our people, their families and the communities in which we operate. We stand by the families of our colleagues and share their grief in this profound loss, as well as their need for answers. We continue to support the Mexican authorities in their ongoing investigation. Our commitment to the families of our colleagues is enduring, as is our belief in Panuco's future and its potential to create lasting opportunities for the communities in Sinaloa and the people of Mexico."

Long-term Support and the Vizsla Foundation 

Since February 2026, Vizsla Silver has been working toward establishing the Vizsla Foundation (the "Foundation") as part of its long-term commitment to the people and communities of Sinaloa. The Foundation is intended to complement the direct assistance the Company continues to provide to the families impacted by the tragic events of January 2026 by focusing on providing meaningful, publicly available, multigenerational support and lasting opportunities to individuals and families across local communities.

The Company continues to engage with the local communities to help shape the Foundation's priorities and long-term initiatives, including support for education, health and economic development in the communities surrounding Panuco. Further details regarding the Foundation's structure and programs will be shared as plans progress and discussions with families continue.

Vizsla Silver has committed to making an initial contribution of US$5 million to the Foundation, with plans to also direct a percentage of future profits toward sustaining its work.

Security and Site Readiness 

The safety of employees and contractors remains central and continues to guide the Company's planning for a return to site. Vizsla Silver continues to work closely with Mexican federal authorities and third-party security advisors to support additional security infrastructure, enhance overall security measures and strengthen on-site support in preparation for a phased return. These efforts build on the Company's established approach to security, which has included a significant investment in security resources, third-party risk assessments and adjustments to or suspension of activities in response to changing conditions. The timing and scope of any formal return to the project site will be informed by the Company's assessment of security conditions and readiness.

Updated Project Guidance 

The Company has revised its targeted first silver production at Panuco to H2 2028, from H2 2027, previously. The revised development schedule reflects the Company's current expectations for permitting, site readiness and construction timing.

Except for the updated development timeline, the Company is not updating the operating, capital or economic parameters disclosed in the Company's November 2025 Feasibility Study (the "Feasibility Study"). The Company has not made a production decision for Panuco (see "No Production Decision" below). GUIYANG, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. ("FTA" or the "Company") (NYSE: YMM), a leading digital freight platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

  • Total net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,585.7 million (US$534.8 million), an increase of 6.8% from RMB3,358.2 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,372.5 million (US$204.7 million), an increase of 49.0% from RMB921.0 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Non-GAAP adjusted net income1 in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,452.8 million (US$216.7 million), an increase of 47.0% from RMB988.1 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Fulfilled orders2 in the third quarter of 2026 reached 70.6 million, an increase of 11.3% from 63.4 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Average shipper MAUs3 in the third quarter of 2026 reached 3.76 million, an increase of 12.4% from 3.35 million in the same period of 2025.

Mr. Peter Hui Zhang, Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer of FTA, commented, "In the third quarter, we continued to grow our user base on both sides of the platform, with particularly strong growth in direct shippers. Efficient cargo finding, together with stronger transaction protection, helped us improve truckers' retention and fulfillment frequency. We also leveraged deeper route-level supply-demand data analysis to upgrade our algorithms, which further improved the overall fulfillment rate. Going forward, we will continue to improve the customer experience through diversified service offerings such as entrusted service for direct shippers, express cargo delivery and top-rated trucker program. We will further integrate AI agents into capacity dispatching across a wider range of routes, further improving fulfillment efficiency. In terms of overseas development, Qmove now operates in five markets, and we will continue to grow its user base and order volume."

Mr. Langbo Guo, President of FTA, added, "Total net revenues reached RMB3.59 billion this quarter, up 6.8% year over year. Transaction service revenues grew steadily, rising 25.0% year over year to RMB1.82 billion. Operating efficiency continued to improve, with net income up 49.0% year over year to RMB1.37 billion and non-GAAP adjusted net income up 47.0% to RMB1.45 billion. Thanks to sustained profit growth and the steady transition of our credit solutions business, net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3.16 billion this quarter, providing us with ample liquidity to support new business initiatives."

1 Non-GAAP adjusted net income is defined as net income excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. See "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

2 Fulfilled orders on our platform in a given period are defined as all shipping orders matched through our platform during such period but exclude (i) shipping orders that are subsequently canceled and (ii) shipping orders for which our users failed to specify any freight prices, as there are substantial uncertainties as to whether such shipping orders are fulfilled.

3 Average shipper MAUs in a given period are calculated by dividing (i) the sum of shipper MAUs for each month of a given period by (ii) the number of months in a given period. Shipper MAUs are defined as the number of active shippers on our platform in a given month. Active shippers are defined as the aggregate number of registered shipper accounts that have posted at least one shipping order on our platform during a given period.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net Revenues (including value added taxes, or "VAT" of RMB1,222.9 million and RMB719.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026, respectively). Total net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,585.7 million (US$534.8 million), representing an increase of 6.8% from RMB3,358.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to an increase in revenues from freight matching services.

Freight matching services. Revenues from freight matching services in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,254.4 million (US$485.4 million), representing an increase of 16.3% from RMB2,797.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly due to the sustained increase in transaction service revenues.

  • Freight brokerage service. Revenues from freight brokerage service in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB1,194.8 million (US$178.2 million), representing an increase of 9.2% from RMB1,094.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to an increase in service fee rate, partially offset by a decrease in transaction volume.

  • Freight listing service. Revenues from freight listing service in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB240.0 million (US$35.8 million), compared with RMB247.1 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decrease in the number of total paying members.

  • Transaction service. Revenues from transaction service amounted to RMB1,819.6 million (US$271.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 25.0% from RMB1,456.1 million in the same period of 2025, primarily driven by increases in order volume, penetration rate and per-order transaction service fee.

Value-added services.4 Revenues from value-added services in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB331.3 million (US$49.4 million), compared with RMB560.7 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in credit solutions revenues.

Cost of Revenues (including VAT net of government grants of RMB1,033.9 million and RMB652.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026, respectively). Cost of revenues in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,026.1 million (US$153.1 million), compared with RMB1,605.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to decreases in VAT, related tax surcharges and other tax costs, net of grants from government authorities. These tax-related costs net of government grants totaled RMB816.8 million, compared with RMB1,427.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decrease in tax costs net of government grants related to the Company's freight brokerage service.

Sales and Marketing Expenses. Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB446.0 million (US$66.5 million), compared with RMB438.8 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to additional investments to support the expansion of the Company's overseas business, partially offset by efficiency-focused spending on domestic user acquisition.

General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB166.8 million (US$24.9 million), compared with RMB161.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher share-based compensation expenses.

Research and Development Expenses. Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB289.8 million (US$43.2 million), compared with RMB233.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly due to ongoing R&D investment in new business initiatives.

Income from Operations. Income from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,609.8 million (US$240.1 million), an increase of 107.4% from RMB776.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP Adjusted Operating Income.5 Non-GAAP adjusted operating income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,683.5 million (US$251.1 million), an increase of 98.3% from RMB849.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Net Income. Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,372.5 million (US$204.7 million), an increase of 49.0% from RMB921.0 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income. Non-GAAP adjusted net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,452.8 million (US$216.7 million), an increase of 47.0% from RMB988.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income per ADS6 and Non-GAAP Adjusted Basic and Diluted Net Income per ADS.7 Basic net income per ADS was RMB1.31 (US$0.20) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.87 in the same period of 2025. Diluted net income per ADS was RMB1.30 (US$0.19) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.87 in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted basic net income per ADS was RMB1.38 (US$0.21) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.94 in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted diluted net income per ADS was RMB1.38 (US$0.21) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.93 in the same period of 2025.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, time deposits and wealth management products of RMB35.5 billion (US$5.3 billion) in total, compared with RMB31.5 billion as of December 31, 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, the total outstanding loan balance8 was RMB2.5 billion (US$0.4 billion), a decrease of 54.4% from RMB5.5 billion as of December 31, 2025. The total non-performing loan ratio8 was 4.7% as of September 30, 2026, compared with 2.9% as of December 31, 2025, primarily due to the migration of previously delinquent balances to outstanding loans that were over 90 calendar days past due, compounded by a rapidly reduced total outstanding loan balance.

In the third quarter of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3,164.2 million (US$471.9 million), compared with RMB1,657.1 million in the same period of 2025. Free cash flow9 was RMB3,040.0 million (US$453.4 million), compared with RMB1,608.5 million in the same period of 2025.

4 The Company provides a range of value-added services including credit solutions, insurance services, electronic toll collection, energy services, intelligent driving-related services, and other services on the FTA platform.

5 Non-GAAP adjusted operating income is defined as income from operations excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions. See "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

6 ADS refers to American depositary shares, each of which represents 20 Class A ordinary shares.

7 Non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per ADS is net income attributable to ordinary shareholders excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments, divided by weighted average number of basic and diluted ADSs, respectively. For more information, refer to "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

8 To better reflect the substance of our credit solutions business and present its complete operating performance, the Company has revised the calculation methodologies of the total outstanding loan balance and the non-performing loan ("NPL") ratio by including off-balance sheet loans in the calculation. Total outstanding loan balance means the aggregate principal amount outstanding under on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet loans as of the end of each reporting period, excluding loans that are more than 180 days past due. Off-balance sheet loans refer to the loans funded by the Company's institutional funding partners for which the Company bears principal risk. NPL ratio is calculated by dividing the sum of total outstanding principal of the on- and off-balance sheet loans that were over 90 calendar days past due (excluding loans that are over 180 days past due and are therefore charged off) by the sum of total outstanding principal of on- and off-balance sheet loans (excluding loans that are over 180 days past due and are therefore charged off) as of a specified date. Comparative periods have been restated accordingly to conform to this presentation.

9 Free cash flow is defined as operating cash flow adjusted for the impact from capital expenditures. Capital expenditures include purchase of property and equipment and intangible assets.

Business Outlook

The Company expects its total net revenues to be between RMB3.19 billion and RMB3.29 billion for the fourth quarter of 2026, representing approximately flat to a 3.1% year-over-year increase. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company uses non-GAAP adjusted operating income, non-GAAP adjusted net income, non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders, non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per share, non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per ADS and free cash flow, each a non-GAAP financial measure, as supplemental measures to review and assess its operating performance.

The presentation of non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted operating income as income from operations excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income as net income excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders as net income attributable to ordinary shareholders excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per share as non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by weighted average number of basic and diluted ordinary shares, respectively. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per ADS as non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of basic and diluted ADSs, respectively. The Company defines free cash flow as operating cash flow adjusted for the impact from capital expenditures. Capital expenditures include purchase of property and equipment and intangible assets.

The non-GAAP financial measures are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as an analytical tool. The non-GAAP financial measures do not reflect all items of expense that affect its operations.

The Company reconciles the non-GAAP financial measures to the nearest U.S. GAAP performance measures. VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / American Critical Minerals Corp. ("American Critical Minerals" or the "Company") (CSE:KCLI)(OTCQB:APCOF)(Frankfurt:2P3) is pleased to announce that it has received assay results from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well, at the Company's Green River Project located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. The highest-grade assay results returned a composite grade of 42.94 weight per cent ("wt.%") KCl over 2.1 metres ("m") (7 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member. Geochemical assay data confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade characteristic of the potash mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and the Paradox Basin.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Assay results and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m or 21.5 feet within the Cycle 5 potash member. High-grade potash with meaningful thickness has now been confirmed at the Green River Project.
  • Results represent an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historic Quintana Fed 1-1 well located 600m (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well 1 .
  • Includes a high composite grade intersection of 42.94 wt.% over 2.1m (6.9 feet).
  • The presence and continuity of sylvite mineralization within the Cycle 5 potash bed now de-risks the historical potash data reported on and available from within the Green River Project.
  • Potash results compare favorably to reported grades from the nearby Moab Solution Mine which produces potash from the same Cycle 5 potash bed 5 .
  • Potash results from the inaugural well on the Green River Project have delivered one of the highest-grade potash intersections globally.

Dean Pekeski, President and CEO stated, "Having completed our inaugural drill program at the Green River Project and we are extremely happy with the results. The potash results are exceptional and highlight the strong pedigree we believed exists within this Property. The significant improvement in both potash grade and thickness versus what was drilled historically validates our targeting exercise and bodes well for future resource delineation. This is a defining moment for our Company and represents the first step in moving this Project forward. Planning for an additional 1-2 wells will commence now with the goal being to generate an NI 43-101 compliant resource and Scoping Study. The Green River Project is progressing while the United States recognizes that critical need for secure fertilizer supply chains."

The Duma Point AP-S-02 Well

The purpose of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well (the "well") was to validate historic drill data and test, through coring and brine sampling, the key Paradox formation potash horizons as well as the clastic brine-bearing zones for lithium and bromine in the Paradox and Leadville formations. Figure 1 shows the location of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well.

Figure 1. - Location map showing the Duma Point AP-S-02 well

Coring operations targeting the Cycle 5 potash member commenced at a depth of 1,741m (5,712 feet) below surface. The core run was planned to recover 45.72m (150 feet) of 4-inch drill core. Due to tight hole conditions causing core loss, core recovery was limited to 25.25m (82.85 feet) with the bottom 20.47 metres (67.15 feet) being lost in the hole. The cored interval did successfully recover 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralization from the Cycle 5 potash member.

To complement the core recovery and aquifer identification, the Company acquired a comprehensive suite of downhole wireline geophysical logs ( "e-logs") to characterize the subsurface stratigraphy and support interpretation of the targeted potash and brine bearing intervals 6 .

The Duma Point AP-S-02 reached a total depth of 2,818 metres (9,245 feet). The well has been cemented and abandoned according to requirements and stipulations found within the State permit for the well, and the drill rig was demobilized on September 25, 2026.

Potash Results

In total, 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralized drill core from the Cycle 5 potash member was recovered (see Figure 2 and Table 1). The downhole wireline geophysical logs show that 1.01m (3.33 feet) of potash mineralized core was lost, meaning that the Cycle 5 potash intersection cut by the well was 6.55m (21.5 feet). In the absence of assays from the lost section of Cycle 5 potash core, downhole wireline geophysical logs results were used to determine the potash content for that interval. 6 There was a strong correlation between the assay results and the downhole wireline geophysical logs for the cored interval.

The vertical well was drilled at Lat: 38.749405, Long: -110.0044758. Based on downhole directional drilling tests and the vertical nature of the stratigraphy interpreted from seismic data the samples are believed to represent true thickness. The 5,794.85-to-5,798.18-foot interval was dropped/lost. Results for this interval are reported from e-logs.

The drill core and completed wireline data confirmed the presence of the Cycle 5 potash unit consistent with historic drilling results from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well, located approximately 0.6 kilometres (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well. The Quintana Fed 1-1 well intersected the Cycle 5 potash bed reporting a grade of 24.3% eKCl from elogs over a thickness of 5.9m (19.4 feet).

Recovered core was logged, photographed, sampled, and transported from Rapid City to the Saskatchewan Research Council laboratories in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, for geochemical analysis. Twenty-one halved core samples were collected and shipped under the supervision of qualified independent geological personnel for analysis using industry-standard procedures. Quality assurance and quality control protocols included the insertion of blanks, standards, and duplicate samples throughout the sampling program. Assays were completed along the entire length of recovered core. Core was also retained for future geo-mechanical testing.

Assays from the recovered drill core returned a composite grade of 35.4 wt.% KCl over 5.54m (18.17 feet) in the Cycle 5 potash member assuming a 5% K 2 O cut-off. Composite carnallite and insoluble content was very low with each reporting <0.1 wt.% and <1.0 wt.% respectively. Included in this assayed interval was a high-grade interval which comprised 2.1m (7 feet) of potash core with a composite grade of 42.94 wt.% KCl (5,780 to 5,787 feet). Table 1 summarizes the assay results from this drill hole.

Figure 2. - Duma Point AP-S-02 photograph of high-grade zone drill core

Adjusting for the lost drill core, the Duma Point AP-S-02 assays and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m (21.5 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member.

Geochemical assay data and grade interpretations from the e-logs confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade character of mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and Paradox Basin. Figure 3 shows how the grade from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well compares with average KCl grades from other potash projects in North America. The intersection reported represents an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historical e-logs from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well.

The Company has no affiliation to any of these Companies or Projects.

Lithium and Bromine Aquifers

Two short-duration drill stem packer tests were completed targeting the Leadville Formation limestone unit (2,670 to 2,815 m or 8,760.2 to 9,236 feet), and lower clastic units of the Paradox Formation (2,144 to 2,181m or 7,035 to 7,155 feet). Although brine was successfully sampled from the Leadville Formation test, meaningful lithium and bromine results were not obtained. Future longer duration pumping tests could provide different results. The sample collected from the Paradox Formation was contaminated with drilling fluids/mud and deemed to be inconclusive. Given these results and the high-cost nature of drilling to these depths, the Company will re-evaluate future drilling and sampling programs within these deep zones.

About American Critical Minerals' Green River Potash and Lithium Project

The Green River Project is situated within Utah's highly productive Paradox Basin, located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. It has significant logistical advantages including close proximity to major rail hubs, airport, roads, water, towns, and labour markets. It also benefits from close proximity to the agricultural and industrial heartland of America and numerous potential end-users for its products.

The history of oil and gas production across the Paradox Basin provides geologic data from historic wells across the Project, and the wider Basin, validating and de-risking the potential for high grade potash and large amounts of contained lithium. Wells in and around the project reported lithium up to 500 ppm, bromine up to 6,100 ppm and boron up to 1,260 ppm (Gilbride & Santos, 2012). This data is reinforced by nearby potash production and the advanced stage of neighbouring lithium projects. The Paradox Basin is believed to be one of the biggest sources of lithium brines in the United States. (Source: AnsonFastmarketsPresentation- https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/pdf/ASN/02823465.pdf ) .1

The Company has disclosed targets for further exploration at the Green River Project consisting of 500 million to 950 million tonnes of sylvinite (the most important source for the production of potash in North America) 4 grading from 12% to 18% potassium oxide based on elog (eK2O=19% to 29% potassium chloride based on elog (eKCl)). Its target for further exploration for Lithium and Bromine is 2.1 billion cubic meters brine volume grading 71.6 to 216.3 ppm Li and 3,656 to 4,741 ppm Br. 2

The Company holds a 100% interest in eleven SITLA mineral and minerals salt leases covering approximately 7,050 acres, 1,094 federal lithium brine claims (BLM Placer Claims) covering 21,150 acres, and 11 federal (BLM) potash prospecting permits covering approximately 25,480 acres. Through these leases, permits and claims the Company has the ability to explore for potash, lithium, and potential by-products across the entire Green River Project (approx. 32,530 acres). The Company is authorized to drill a total of 7 drill holes across the Green River Project.

America's largest potash company and only U.S. domestic potash producer currently produces potash from its nearby Moab Solution Mine, which the Company believes provides strong evidence of stratigraphic continuity within this part of the Paradox Basin 5 . Anson Resources Ltd. has advanced lithium development projects contiguous to the northern boundary of our Green River Project and neighbouring to the south. 5 Anson has a large initial resource, robust definitive feasibility study and has recently completed successful piloting operations through its partnership with Koch Technology Solutions, as well as an offtake agreement with LG Energy Solution. The Anson exploration targets encompass the combined Mississippian Leadville Formation and the Pennsylvanian Paradox Formation brine-bearing clastic layers, which also underlie American Critical Minerals' entire project area (www.ansonresources.com). 3

The United States imports more than 90% of its potash demand (U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2025). In November 2025, the Department of Interior added potash to its list of Critical Minerals which already includes lithium. Recent market estimates suggest that the global potash market is over US$50 billion annually and growing at a compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") of close to 5%. Annual lithium demand is now estimated to be over 1 million tonnes globally and continuing to grow rapidly. 4

The scientific and technical content of this news release has been reviewed, verified, and approved by Dean Besserer, P.Geo., the Chief Operations Officer of the Company and a qualified person for the purposes of NI 43-101.

Targets for further exploration for potash, lithium and bromine at the Green River Project are used to provide a conceptual estimate of the potential quantity and grade of a mineral deposit, based on known and additional limited geological evidence. It is an early-stage assessment that will help to guide further exploration, but it is not a mineral resource or mineral reserve and should not be treated as such. The report titled "Amended and Restated NI 43-101 Technical Report, Green River Potash and Lithium Project, Grand County, USA' dated January 27, 2026, and available under the Company's profile at www.sedarplus.ca provides details of the basis on which the targets for further exploration have been determined.

3 American Critical Minerals' management cautions that results or discoveries on properties in proximity to the American Critical Minerals' properties may not necessarily be indicative of the presence of mineralization on the Company's properties.

4 United States Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/mcs2024-potash.pdf ).

5 The Company has no affiliation to Intrepid Potash or the Moab Mine or Anson Resources.

6 Downhole geophysical logs may be used to identify the presence of potash. Naturally occurring radioactivity derived from the potassium in the potash beds give a characteristic gamma ray signature that is commonly used in the industry to estimate grade. The correlation between gamma ray response and potassium content was chiefly advanced by Schlumberger, beginning in the 1960s with the interpretation of elogs in the Prairie Evaporite Formation in Saskatchewan. Schlumberger furthered this work and related log response to apparent K 2 O content. Alibaba E-commerce Group

Recent progress includes the integration of management across our domestic and international wholesale businesses, as well as the launch of QwenWork E-commerce for merchants, an AI product powered by our agentic AI capabilities, in October.

QwenWork E-commerce is integrated into QwenWork, our one-stop AI agent platform, and is designed to automate end-to-end merchant workflows, including store operations, business analytics, advertising and customer service. Leveraging our existing merchant tools, it connects directly to Taobao and Tmall data and will further support data access across other platforms, enabling more seamless cross-platform operations. In addition, by leveraging Qwen model family’s advanced multimodal capabilities, we are able to better understand complex consumer needs and deliver more relevant product recommendations with knowledge-based reasoning. These enhanced capabilities have driven a notable increase in general knowledge-related queries, creating more opportunities to identify latent consumer demand, facilitate product discovery, and drive sales conversion.

In our China Quick Commerce business, Taobao Instant Commerce continued to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter while maintaining market share. This reflected higher average order value, as we further improved the order mix through an increasing focus on high-value food and non-food categories. Meanwhile, Freshippo maintained its robust growth across online and offline channels, driven by deeper collaboration with Taobao Instant Commerce and the expansion of its multi-format store network that offers differentiated products to diverse demographics.

The number of 88VIP members, our highest spending consumer group, continued to increase by double digits year-over-year to approximately 66 million as of September 30, 2026. The ARPU of new 88VIP members, defined as those who joined the membership program within the past year, increased significantly year-over-year during the 11.11 Global Shopping Festival. We remain focused on the growth and retention of 88VIP members through enhanced value proposition to our most valued customers.

Xianyu is China’s leading consumer-to-consumer community and marketplace for idle goods. It makes buying and selling more convenient for consumers and small businesses through AI-powered features including smart pricing, automated product listing descriptions and precise buyer targeting, as well as consignment services. This quarter, Xianyu continued its strong growth momentum, with daily active users and paid orders up 23% and 29% year-over-year, respectively.

AI Cloud and Compute Services

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services was RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), a 53% increase from the same quarter last year. The growth of revenue from external customers accelerated to 64% year-over-year. The growth of recurring revenue from external customers, which excludes compute equipment solutions revenue, also accelerated to 67% year-over-year. In particular, AI-related product revenue continued to show strong momentum, achieving RMB17,918 million (US$2,673 million) and delivering the thirteenth consecutive quarter of triple-digit year-over-year growth. The strong growth reflected broad-based demand for our AI + Cloud services. Beyond training and inference workloads at AI labs, customers across the internet, automotive, embodied AI, financial services and biotechnology sectors rapidly expanded their use of our cloud services to support innovation and grow their business.

Cloud

Alibaba Cloud continued to strengthen our market-leading full-stack AI capabilities, as demonstrated by the comprehensive upgrades unveiled at the Apsara Conference in September, spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. These advancements across our co-designed and integrated stack have accelerated enterprise adoption and deeper integration into core business workflows, enabling us to capitalize on increasingly diverse demand across industries.

Our ability to empower enterprise AI adoption has earned notable recognition in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Strategic Cloud Platform Services, a report that comprehensively evaluates how cloud service providers support the entire enterprise cloud lifecycle. Alibaba Cloud was named a Leader in the highest quadrant, making it the first and only Asia-Pacific provider to receive this distinction.

Chip Design – T-Head Semiconductor (“T-Head”)

By rapidly advancing its portfolio of proprietary chips and software, T-Head further strengthened the infrastructure foundation underpinning our AI capabilities.

At the Apsara Conference in September, we unveiled the Zhenwu V900, our next-generation AI chip for training and inference, with commercial release scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Built on our proprietary parallel computing architecture, the Zhenwu V900 delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, the Zhenwu M890. We also open-sourced T-Head SAIL, the software stack for Zhenwu chips, to simplify application migration, expand developer adoption, and strengthen compatibility with mainstream AI frameworks.

In addition, we launched the Zhenwu M890 supernode instance in August, marking the introduction of China’s first supernode architecture capable of supporting inference for models with more than two trillion parameters. At the Apsara Conference, we also showcased our next-generation supernode product, which integrates the Zhenwu V900 with other proprietary interconnect, networking, and storage chips, and is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2027.

AI Labs and Applications

Model

We continued to advance our comprehensive model portfolio, with a primary focus on foundation models, while enhancing capabilities across video, audio, image and music. This demonstrates our industry leadership and rapid pace of iteration.

Recently, we launched Qwen4-Max, built on the new mixture-of-experts architecture with 2.4 trillion backbone parameters and native visual capabilities. Qwen4-Max advances productivity and token efficiency, delivering stronger long-horizon task execution across industries, including manufacturing, game development, healthcare, and frontier scientific research.

QwenWork

Our agentic platform QwenWork continued to gain traction across industries, driven by ongoing enhancements to its enterprise capabilities. At the Apsara Conference in September, we launched Enterprise Context, a solution that continuously organizes and updates enterprise information and knowledge across company documents, meeting records and internal communications. It enables AI agents to access company-specific information and execute tasks based on organizational knowledge and workflows.

Qwen App

Qwen app for individual users now provides personalized assistance for tasks across more than 20 service categories, including shopping, local services, travel, work, learning, personal finance and health, leveraging Alibaba’s ecosystem and third-party partnerships. In October, we launched Qwen Go!, a cloud-based personal agent embedded within the Qwen app. Qwen Go! autonomously executes multi-step tasks across platforms, while retaining contextual information and user preferences over time to deliver increasingly personalized assistance across everyday activities.

All Others

Our store guide and mapping platform Amap offers consumers one-stop access to services such as navigation, to-destination services and ride-hailing. On October 1, 2026, the first day of National Day holiday in China, Amap recorded an all-time high of approximately 370 million peak daily active users. Leveraging Amap Street Stars, a feature that provides a trust-based rating system to support users’ consumption decisions, Amap has strengthened its mindshare in local services across consumption use cases, including dining, tourist attractions and seasonal activities.

Share Repurchases

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased a total of 17.95 million ordinary shares (equivalent to approximately 2.24 million ADSs) for a total of US$221 million. These purchases were made in the U.S. market under our share repurchase program.

Capital Expenditures

During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, capital expenditures were RMB50,477 million (US$7,529 million), an increase of 60% compared to RMB31,501 million in the same quarter of 2025, due to continued investments in AI infrastructure to meet strong and accelerating customer demand. The significant year-over-year increase was due to an acceleration in scaling compute capacity, higher pricing of a broad range of chip components, an increase in CPU-compute capacity driven by anticipated growing customer adoption of AI agents, and fluctuations in procurement cycles.

In addition to training and inference demand from AI Labs, we continue to see robust demand from customers in China’s emerging innovation economy, including electric vehicles (EVs), embodied AI, and biotechnology. Scale is becoming an increasingly critical competitive advantage in cloud computing, providing us with orchestration flexibility, operating efficiency and cost advantages. By investing in infrastructure today, we aim to extend our scale leadership, strengthen our supply chain and reinforce our long-term competitive position.

NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES

To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP, we use the following non-GAAP financial measures: for our consolidated results, adjusted EBITDA (including adjusted EBITDA margin), adjusted EBITA (including adjusted EBITA margin), non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow. For more information on these non-GAAP financial measures, please refer to the table captioned “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Measures to the Nearest Comparable U.S. GAAP Measures” in this results announcement.

We believe that adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS help identify underlying trends in our business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain income or expenses that we include in income from operations, net income and diluted earnings per share/ADS. We believe that these non-GAAP measures provide useful information about our core operating results, enhance the overall understanding of our past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by our management in its financial and operational decision-making. We present three different income measures, namely adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA and non-GAAP net income in order to provide more information and greater transparency to investors about our operating results.

We consider free cash flow to be a liquidity measure that provides useful information to management and investors about the amount of cash generated by our business that can be used for strategic corporate transactions, including investing in our new business initiatives, making strategic investments and acquisitions and strengthening our balance sheet.

Adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EBITA, non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP diluted earnings per share/ADS and free cash flow should not be considered in isolation or construed as an alternative to income from operations, net income, diluted earnings per share/ADS, cash flows or any other measure of performance or as an indicator of our operating performance. These non-GAAP financial measures presented here do not have standardized meanings prescribed by U.S. GAAP and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures presented by other companies. Other companies may calculate similarly titled measures differently, limiting their usefulness as comparative measures to our data.

Adjusted EBITDA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, depreciation and impairment of property and equipment, and operating lease cost relating to land use rights, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Adjusted EBITA represents net income before interest and investment income, net, interest expense, other income (expense), net, income tax expenses, share of results of equity method investees, certain non-cash expenses, consisting of share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, impairment of goodwill, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), which we do not believe are reflective of our core operating performance during the periods presented.

Non-GAAP net income represents net income before non-cash share-based compensation expense, amortization and impairment of intangible assets, gain or loss on deemed disposals/disposals/revaluation of investments, impairment of goodwill and investments, and others (including provision in relation to matters outside the ordinary course of business), and adjustments for the tax effects.

Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share represents non-GAAP net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of outstanding ordinary shares, in each case for computing non-GAAP diluted earnings per share on a diluted basis. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS represents non-GAAP diluted earnings per share after adjusting for the ordinary share-to-ADS ratio.

Free cash flow represents net cash provided by operating activities as presented in our consolidated cash flow statement less purchases of property and equipment (excluding acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses) and intangible assets (excluding those acquired through acquisitions), as well as adjustments to exclude from net cash provided by operating activities the buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces. We deduct certain items of cash flows from investing activities in order to provide greater transparency into cash flow from our revenue-generating business operations. We exclude “acquisition of land use rights and construction in progress relating to office campuses” because the office campuses are used by us for corporate and administrative purposes and are not directly related to our revenue-generating business operations. We also exclude buyer protection fund deposits from merchants on our marketplaces because these deposits are restricted for the purpose of compensating buyers for claims against merchants.

The table captioned “Reconciliations of Non-GAAP Measures to the Nearest Comparable U.S. GAAP Measures” in this results announcement has more details on the non-GAAP financial measures that are most directly comparable to GAAP financial measures and the related reconciliations between these financial measures.

ebitafinancial
EBITA stands for Earnings Before Interest, Taxes and Amortization and measures a company’s profit from operations after removing the effects of financing, tax rules and amortization charges. For investors, ads matter because they drive sales growth, affect how much a company must spend to win customers, and influence brand strength and long-term value. Ads can also create regulatory or reputational risk if claims are misleading, which can affect profits and stock price.

HAMBURG, Germany, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Evotec SE (NASDAQ: EVO) (Frankfurt Prime Standard: EVT) today announced that its strategic protein degradation partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb has received a second Investigational New Drug (IND) acceptance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). The first candidate produced under the partnership entered a Phase 1 clinical trial in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma in March 2026. The second accepted investigational drug candidate, a cereblon E3 ligase modulator (CELMoD), is expected to enter a Phase 1 clinical trial in 2027.

Initiated in 2018, the partnership combines Evotec's high-performance multi-omics screening, AI-supported data analytics, and drug design capabilities with Bristol Myers Squibb's industry-leading CELMoD agent library. This collaboration, expanded in 2022, continues to advance a pipeline of novel molecular glue degraders for high-value targets in oncology and beyond, translating scientific innovation into a growing therapeutic pipeline.

Dr. Joanna Holbrook, Chief Scientific Officer of Evotec, commented:

"The progression of a second molecular glue candidate to IND acceptance demonstrates the repeatability and productivity of our discovery platform. We are systematically translating complex biology into development candidates. This achievement reinforces the value of our longstanding collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and further strengthens our confidence in the platform's potential to generate a growing pipeline of investigational drug candidates aimed at addressing substantial unmet medical needs."

About molecular glue degraders

Conventional small molecule therapeutics act through drug-induced interference with protein activity. This limitation to agonistic or antagonistic functions renders about 90% of proteins 'undruggable'. Also, conventional small molecules only work while they are actively binding to the receptor, which typically requires a treatment regimen consisting of one or even several carefully dosed medications every day.

Molecular glue degraders are compounds that induce interactions between an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a molecular target. The induced interaction results in ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of the recruited protein. By inducing neomorphic interactions between CRBN and substrate proteins, CELMoDs enable pharmacological modulation of proteins that may not be amenable to traditional inhibitor or agonist approaches, thereby expanding the potentially druggable proteome.

About Evotec's strategic collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb in molecular glues

In 2018, Evotec entered a long-term strategic drug discovery and development collaboration in the field of molecular glues with Celgene, now Bristol Myers Squibb. Bristol Myers Squibb is a leader in this field based on its unique library of CELMoD agents. The collaboration aims to discover and develop a leading pipeline of molecular glue degraders for a range of therapeutic indications leveraging all of Evotec's proprietary PanOmics and PanHunter platforms as well as AI/ML-based drug discovery and development capabilities.

Evotec applies high-end proteomics and transcriptomics at industrial scale to profile and select promising drug candidates based on comprehensive cell biological profiles. Evotec's leading PanOmics screening capabilities are delivering unmatched throughput. The selection of the most promising candidates for drug development is facilitated by Evotec's PanOmics data analysis platform PanHunter. By integrating and analyzing these data sets, PanHunter supports the identification and advancement of the most promising CELMoDs into lead optimization.

About Evotec SE

Evotec is a life science company pioneering the future of drug discovery and development. By integrating breakthrough science with AI-driven innovation and advanced technologies, Evotec accelerates the journey from concept to cure with greater speed, intelligence and precision. The company's expertise spans small molecules, biologics, cell therapies and associated modalities, supported by proprietary platforms including Molecular Patient Databases, PanOmics and induced pluripotent stem cell-based disease modeling. Through flexible partnering models tailored to customers' needs, Evotec works with all Top 20 pharmaceutical companies, more than 800 biotechnology companies, academic institutions and other healthcare stakeholders. Evotec's offerings range from standalone services to fully integrated research and development programs and long-term strategic partnerships, combining scientific excellence with operational agility. Through Just - Evotec Biologics, the company is redefining biologics development and manufacturing to improve accessibility and affordability. With a portfolio of more than 100 proprietary research and development assets, most of which are co-owned, Evotec focuses on key therapeutic areas including oncology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurology and immunology. Evotec's global team of around 4,500 experts operates from sites in Europe and the United States, providing complementary technologies and services through a network of synergistic centers of excellence. Learn more at www.evotec.com and follow Evotec on LinkedIn and X at @Evotec.

MT. LAUREL, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--InTest Corporation (NYSE American: INTT), a global supplier of innovative test and process technology solutions, today announced the launch of the BT-28 ECO, a next-generation benchtop air forcing system from InTest Thermal Solutions. Designed to meet and exceed the requirements of European Union Regulation (EU) 2024/573, the BT-28 ECO advances precision thermal testing while helping customers respond to a rapidly changing refrigerant and sustainability landscape.

“We designed the BT-28 ECO to meet emerging European F-gas requirements without asking customers to give up speed, accuracy, workspace or ease of use. It is a strong example of our commitment to helping customers boost performance while preparing their operations for a more sustainable future,” said Scott Taylor, Vice President and General Manager of InTest’s Environmental Technologies division.

“The BT-28 ECO shows how InTest’s leadership and focus on innovation in precision temperature control translate into value-creating solutions for our customers,” added Rich Rogoff, President and Chief Executive Officer of InTest Corporation.

The BT-28 ECO delivers a temperature range of -28°C to +225°C utilizing refrigerants with a GWP less than 5.0. It transitions from -10°C to +125°C, and back, in approximately 10 seconds or less, while providing 14 scfm (6.5 l/s) airflow across the full temperature range. The system delivers temperature resolution of ±0.1°C and temperature accuracy of 1.0°C when calibrated against a NIST standard.

Engineered for laboratories and production environments where floor and bench space are at a premium, the portable system measures approximately 13.9 inches wide by 23.4 inches deep by 16.7 inches high and weighs approximately 80 pounds. Its ECO-Stream design is smaller, quieter and more energy-efficient, with operating sound levels below 60 dBA and below 50 dBA at idle.

BT-28 ECO Highlights

Regulatory readiness
Designed to meet and exceed EU 2024/573 requirements and support the transition to lower-GWP refrigerants.

Industry-leading benchtop performance
Fast transitions, 14 scfm airflow and a -28°C to +225°C operating range.

Compact, quiet operation
Portable benchtop footprint with <60 dBA operation and <50 dBA at idle.

Flexible control
Detachable touchscreen with a 9-foot (3-meter) remote cable and proprietary direct DUT temperature control.

Serviceability and safety
Auto-diagnostics, field-replaceable modules and operator-set high and low temperature limits.

 

The detachable touchscreen can be positioned within the reach of the supplied remote cable, giving operators greater flexibility around the test area. Available accessories include thermal caps, bench clamps, a control cradle, tall and short carts, custom enclosures and non-conductive mats.

About InTest Thermal Solutions

InTest Thermal Solutions specializes in the design and manufacture of thermal test, process cooling and biomedical cold storage systems. Its product portfolio and in-house engineering capabilities provide precision temperature control solutions for demanding environments ranging from -185°C to +500°C, with rapid transitions or long dwell times. InTest Thermal Solutions is a wholly owned subsidiary of InTest Corporation.

InTest Corporation is a global supplier of innovative test and process technology solutions for use in manufacturing and testing across a wide range of markets, including automotive, defense/aerospace, industrial, life sciences, semiconductor and telecommunications. Backed by decades of engineering expertise and a culture of operational excellence, InTest solves difficult thermal, mechanical and electronic challenges for customers worldwide. Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Epic Gold Corp. (CSE: EPG) (the "Company") is pleased to announce the completion of an initial independent Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE") for its Wilson Gold Project (the "Wilson Project" or the "Project"), located in Québec, Canada.

The initial MRE defines an Inferred Mineral Resource of 3.047 million tonnes grading 2.85 grams per tonne ("g/t") gold ("Au"), containing approximately 279,000 ounces of gold, within optimized open-pit and underground reporting constraints.

The estimate establishes an initial mineral resource inventory for the Wilson Project and provides a technical foundation for ongoing geological interpretation, resource evaluation and exploration planning.

Highlights of the Initial Wilson Mineral Resource Estimate

  • 279,000 ounces of gold contained in 3.047 million tonnes grading 2.85 g/t Au in the Inferred Mineral Resource category.
  • Mineral Resources reported within open-pit and underground constraints.
  • Reporting cut-off grades of 0.40 g/t Au (open pit) and 1.60 g/t Au (underground).

The MRE has an effective date of November 9, 2026, and incorporates historical drilling, assay results, geological interpretation and three-dimensional mineralization modelling.

HONG KONG, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Futu Holdings Limited (“Futu” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: FUTU), a leading tech-driven online brokerage and wealth management platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Operational Highlights

  • Total number of funded accounts1 increased 27.9% year-over-year to 4,005,858 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of brokerage accounts2 increased 22.5% year-over-year to 6,868,829 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of users3 increased 13.8% year-over-year to 32.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total client assets increased 7.6% year-over-year to HK$1.33 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
  • Daily average client assets were HK$1.33 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 21.1% from the same period in 2025.
  • Total trading volume in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 28.4% year-over-year to HK$5.01 trillion, in which trading volume for U.S. stocks was HK$3.81 trillion, and trading volume for Hong Kong stocks was HK$942.5 billion.
  • Margin financing and securities lending balance increased 17.1% year-over-year to HK$73.8 billion as of September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights 

  • Total revenues increased 4.5% year-over-year to HK$6,690.6 million (US$852.7 million). 
  • Total gross profit was largely stable year-over-year to HK$5,630.5 million (US$717.6 million).
  • Net income was largely stable year-over-year to HK$3,186.7 million (US$406.1 million). 
  • Non-GAAP adjusted net income⁴ was largely stable year-over-year to HK$3,272.4 million (US$417.0 million).

Mr. Leaf Hua Li, Futu’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said, “While equity market conditions softened during the past quarter and investor sentiment became more cautious, our business remained resilient. During the quarter, we deepened our relationships with clients, broadened our multi-asset product capabilities, and continued to diversify our geographic mix and revenue base. These developments reinforce our confidence in the direction of our long-term strategy, while we remain focused on disciplined execution.”

“As of quarter-end, our total funded accounts reached 4.0 million, up 27.9% year-over-year. We added 163 thousand net new funded accounts in the quarter despite challenging equity markets and mixed news across certain regions. Excluding mainland China and Japan, net new funded accounts would have been approximately 173 thousand. International markets remain primary growth engine, with Malaysia contributing the largest number of net new funded account additions, followed by Singapore and Hong Kong, reflecting a diversified geographic profile of growth. Our average client retention rate remained above 98%, showing our ability to support clients through changing market conditions and evolving investment needs.”

“We delivered resilient net asset inflows of approximately HK$34.5 billion during the quarter despite challenging market conditions, supported by an expanding product suite and deeper customer engagement. Total client assets were HK$1.33 trillion as of quarter end, up 7.6% year-over-year and down 4.6% quarter-over-quarter. The sequential decline was primarily attributable to lower market valuations. Margin financing and securities lending balance declined 22.3% quarter-over-quarter to HK$73.8 billion, largely reflecting a high comparison base in the prior quarter, while remaining higher year-over-year.”

“Our strategic transition towards a broader wealth management platform gained traction during the quarter. Client assets in wealth management increased 11.8% year-over-year and 9.0% quarter-over-quarter to HK$196.4 billion. During the quarter, clients rotated into money market funds amid a more cautious investment sentiment. We further broadened our product offering with two Hong Kong market firsts: a weekly-dealing public mutual fund and a fully tokenized gold ETF. To meet the increasingly sophisticated trading and asset allocation needs of high-net-worth clients, we launched over-the-counter derivatives trading in Hong Kong and introduced a wholesale fund in Malaysia. Our AI assistant has also expanded into wealth management, supporting clients throughout the investment process, from portfolio analysis and fund selection to ongoing monitoring. As a result, wealth management penetration climbed to 28.2%, representing 1.13 million customers.”

“Total trading volume was HK$5.01 trillion, up 28.4% year-over-year and down 22.0% quarter-over-quarter, as softer equity market conditions, particularly a sharp pullback in semiconductor and AI-related names, dampened client trading activity. U.S. stock trading volume declined 24.0% sequentially to HK$3.81 trillion. Hong Kong stock trading volume declined 19.2% quarter-over-quarter to HK$942.5 billion.”

“Amid continued strength in Hong Kong’s IPO market, we provided IPO-related services to more than 70% of new listings and served as joint bookrunners for several prominent IPOs, including those of Momenta, Longsys, and Mech-Mind Robotics.”

“Despite near-term volatility across global equity markets, we remain confident in our long-term outlook. Rising investable wealth across Asia, growing demand for multi-asset allocation, and continued adoption of digital financial services remain long-term growth drivers. Our priorities remain clear: deepening client relationships, expanding our wealth management capabilities and strengthening our international franchise, laying the foundation for sustainable growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Total revenues were HK$6,690.6 million (US$852.7 million), an increase of 4.5% from HK$6,402.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HK$2,793.9 million (US$356.1 million), a decrease of 4.1% from the third quarter of 2025. This was mainly due to the decrease in blended commission rate from 7.5bps to 5.6bps, partially offset by the 28.4% year-over-year increase in total trading volume.

Interest income was HK$3,161.8 million (US$403.0 million), an increase of 3.8% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was mainly driven by higher interest income from margin financing and bank deposit, largely offset by the decrease in interest income from securities borrowing and lending business. 

Other income was HK$734.8 million (US$93.6 million), an increase of 65.5% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher currency exchange income and fund distribution service income. 

Costs

Total costs were HK$1,060.0 million (US$135.1million), an increase of 33.6% compared to HK$793.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Brokerage commission and handling charge expenses were HK$238.8 million (US$30.4 million), an increase of 48.7% from the third quarter of 2025. This increase was mainly driven by the growth of trading volume. 

Interest expenses were HK$585.6 million (US$74.6 million), an increase of 23.6% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher expenses associated with our margin financing.

Processing and servicing costs were HK$235.6 million (US$30.0 million), an increase of 48.0% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to increasing cloud service fees. 

Gross Profit

Total gross profit was HK$5,630.5 million (US$717.6 million), largely stable from HK$5,609.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Gross margin was 84.2%, as compared to 87.6% in the third quarter of 2025. 

Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses were HK$1,590.4 million (US$202.7 million), a decrease of 6.7% from HK$1,704.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Research and development expenses were HK$483.9 million (US$61.7 million), a decrease of 15.7% from the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to effective cost-control measures.

Selling and marketing expenses were HK$545.1 million (US$69.5 million), a decrease of 6.9% from HK$585.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to fewer net new funded accounts in the quarter.

General and administrative expenses were HK$561.4 million (US$71.5 million), an increase of 3.0% from HK$545.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was mainly driven by higher office rental expenses.

Income from Operations

Income from operations increased by 3.5% to HK$4,040.1 million (US$514.9 million) from HK$3,904.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. Operating margin was 60.4%, largely stable compared to 61.0% in the third quarter of 2025. 

Net Income

Net income was largely stable at HK$3,186.7million (US406.1 million) from HK$3,217.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net income margin for the third quarter of 2026 declined to 47.6% from 50.2% in the year-ago quarter.

Non-GAAP adjusted net income was largely stable at HK$3,272.4 million (US$417.0 million) from the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted net income is defined as net income excluding share-based compensation expenses. For further information, see "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" at the bottom of this press release.

Net Income per ADS

Basic net income per American Depositary Share ("ADS") was HK$23.36 (US$2.98), compared with HK$23.20 in the third quarter of 2025. Diluted net income per ADS was HK$23.20 (US$2.96), compared with HK$22.80 in the third quarter of 2025. Each ADS represents eight Class A ordinary shares.
