About Futu Holdings Limited

Futu Holdings Limited (Nasdaq: FUTU) is an advanced technology company transforming the investing experience by offering fully digitalized financial services. Through its proprietary digital platforms, Futubull and Moomoo, the Company provides a full range of investment services, including trade execution and clearing, margin financing and securities lending, and wealth management. The Company has embedded social media tools to create a network centered around its users and provide connectivity to users, investors, companies, analysts, media and key opinion leaders. The Company also provides corporate services, including IPO distribution, investor relations and ESOP solution services.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In evaluating the business, the Company considers and uses non-GAAP adjusted net income, a non-GAAP measure, as a supplemental measure to review and assess its operating performance. The presentation of the non-GAAP financial measure is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income as net income excluding share-based compensation expenses. The Company presents the non-GAAP financial measure because it is used by the management to evaluate the operating performance and formulate business plans. Non-GAAP adjusted net income enables the management to assess the Company's operating results without considering the impact of share-based compensation expenses, which are non-cash charges. The Company also believes that the use of the non-GAAP measure facilitates investors' assessment of its operating performance.

Non-GAAP adjusted net income is not defined under U.S. GAAP and is not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. This non-GAAP financial measure has limitations as analytical tools. One of the key limitations of using non-GAAP adjusted net income is that it does not reflect all items of expense that affect the Company's operations. Share-based compensation expenses have been and may continue to be incurred in the business and is not reflected in the presentation of non-GAAP adjusted net income. Further, the non-GAAP measure may differ from the non-GAAP information used by other companies, including peer companies, and therefore their comparability may be limited.

The Company compensates for these limitations by reconciling the non-GAAP financial measure to the nearest U.S. GAAP performance measure, all of which should be considered when evaluating the Company's performance.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Prospect Prediction Markets Inc. (TSXV: MKT) (OTCQB: MKTSF) (FSE: DEP) ("Prospect Markets" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that Mr. Kevin Gopaul has been nominated for election to the Company's board of directors at its upcoming annual general meeting of shareholders (the "Meeting"), scheduled to be held on December 30, 2026.

Mr. Gopaul currently serves as a strategic advisor to the Company. If elected, he will bring nearly 30 years of experience in capital markets and asset management, including senior leadership roles in the Canadian exchange-traded fund industry.

"Kevin built one of Canada's leading ETF businesses from scratch. He knows how to launch new products, earn the trust of institutions and regulators, and hold a company to the highest governance standards. That's exactly the experience we need on our board as we scale following our U.S. launch."

"I'm pleased to be nominated for election to the board of Prospect Markets. Having worked with the team as a strategic advisor, I look forward to contributing my experience to support the Company's next phase of growth," said Kevin Gopaul.

About Mr. Gopaul

Mr. Gopaul has nearly 30 years of experience in the investment management industry, spanning research, trading, portfolio management and executive leadership. He has been Chief Executive Officer of VanEck Canada Inc. since April 2026.

Before that, he spent more than 14 years at BMO Global Asset Management, where he helped build BMO Exchange Traded Funds from its inception into one of Canada's leading ETF businesses, surpassing $100 billion in assets. His roles at BMO included Global Head of Exchange Traded Funds, CEO and Country Head for Canada, and Chief Investment Officer for Canada, overseeing investment teams in Hong Kong, London and Chicago.

Earlier in his career, Mr. Gopaul held senior roles with Barclays Global Investors, Scotia Capital and Sun Life Financial, working across both institutional and retail investor channels.

Mr. Gopaul has been an active contributor to the Canadian financial services industry. He was the founding and longest-serving director of the Canadian ETF Association (CETFA) and has served on the Public Policy Committee of the Canadian Coalition for Good Governance (CCGG).

Mr. Gopaul's appointment as a director is subject to shareholder approval at the Meeting and applicable regulatory requirements.

About Prospect Markets

Prospect Markets is the prediction market platform built natively for sports. From the world's largest leagues to niche competitions, Prospect turns every sports moment into a tradable market. Fans trade peer-to-peer on outcomes using real-time data from our second-screen experience which transforms passive viewership into active market participation.

BEIJING, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG) (“Sunlands” or the “Company”), a leader in China’s adult online education market and China’s adult personal interest learning market, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Snapshots

  • Net revenues were RMB331.6 million (US$49.5 million), compared to RMB523.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross billings (non-GAAP) were RMB239.0 million (US$35.6 million), compared to RMB349.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million), compared to RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income margin1 was 10.6%, compared to 24.0% in the third quarter of 2025.
  • New student enrollments2 were 84,879, compared to 137,493 in the third quarter of 2025.
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s deferred revenue balance was RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

_____________________________

1 Net income margin is defined as net income as a percentage of net revenues.
2 New student enrollments for a given period refer to the total number of orders placed by students that newly enroll in at least one course during that period, including those students that enroll and then terminate their enrollment with us, excluding orders of our low-price courses, such as “mini courses” and “RMB1 courses”, which we offer in the form of recorded videos or short live streaming, to strengthen our competitiveness and improve customer experience.

Mr. Tongbo Liu, Chief Executive Officer of Sunlands, commented, “During the third quarter of 2026, we remained focused on our core business, refining our course offerings and teaching services to better address evolving learner needs. As demand for lifelong learning among middle-aged and senior learners continues to diversify, we are placing greater emphasis on course quality, personalized learning experiences, and long-term learner engagement. Looking ahead, we will continue to build on our experience in adult education, further integrate technology into teaching and services, and strengthen our core business to support sustainable development.”

Mr. Hangyu Li, Finance Director of Sunlands, added, “In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues were RMB331.6 million and net income was RMB35.2 million, representing net income margin of 10.6%. Against a lower revenue base, we reduced operating expenses by 25.3% year-over-year and remained profitable for the 22nd consecutive quarter. We remain focused on aligning costs and resource allocation with our operating needs, preserving liquidity, and allocating capital prudently to support our core business and long-term development.”

Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

Net Revenues

In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues decreased by 36.6% to RMB331.6 million (US$49.5 million) from RMB523.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 3.6% to RMB58.1 million (US$8.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB60.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 40.9% to RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the third quarter of 2026, operating expenses were RMB242.2 million (US$36.1 million), representing a 25.3% decrease from RMB324.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 26.4% to RMB206.0 million (US$30.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB279.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 18.7% to RMB29.2 million (US$4.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB36.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 18.9% to RMB7.0 million (US$1.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB8.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined compensation expenses related to the Company’s product development personnel.

Net Income

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), as compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB5.53 (US$0.83) in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to RMB18.64 in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash, Cash Equivalents, Restricted Cash and Short-term Investments

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had RMB502.0 million (US$74.9 million) of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB281.4 million (US$42.0 million) of short-term investments, as compared to RMB576.8 million of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB235.9 million of short-term investments as of December 31, 2025.

Deferred Revenue

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a deferred revenue balance of RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), as compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

Share Repurchase

On May 29, 2026, the Company’s board of directors authorized a share repurchase program, under which the Company may repurchase up to US$50.0 million of Class A ordinary shares in the form of ADSs over the next 36 months. As of November 17, 2026, the Company had repurchased an aggregate of 716,479 ADSs for approximately US$2.4 million under the share repurchase program.

Financial Results for the First Nine Months of 2026

Net Revenues

In the first nine months of 2026, net revenues decreased by 23.9% to RMB1,178.6 million (US$175.8 million) from RMB1,549.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 13.6% to RMB174.9 million (US$26.1 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB202.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined cost of revenues from sales of goods such as learning materials and books and decreased service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 25.5% to RMB1,003.7 million (US$149.7 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB1,347.4 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the first nine months of 2026, operating expenses were RMB792.2 million (US$118.2 million), representing a 21.4% decrease from RMB1,008.1 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 23.4% to RMB676.2 million (US$100.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB882.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 6.4% to RMB96.9 million (US$14.5 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB103.6 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 12.5% to RMB19.1 million (US$2.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB21.9 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Net Income

Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB195.5 million (US$29.2 million), compared with RMB327.3 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB29.79 (US$4.44) in the first nine months of 2026, compared with RMB48.50 in the first nine months of 2025.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Sunlands currently expects net revenues to be between RMB220 million to RMB240 million, which would represent a decrease of between 49.0% to 53.2% year-over-year. The above outlook is based on the current market conditions and reflects the Company’s current and preliminary estimates of market and operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to substantial uncertainty.

Exchange Rate

The Company’s business is primarily conducted in China and all revenues are denominated in Renminbi (“RMB”). This announcement contains currency conversions of RMB amounts into U.S. dollars (“US$”) solely for the convenience of the reader. Unless otherwise noted, all translations from RMB to US$ are made at a rate of RMB6.7045 to US$1.00, the effective noon buying rate for September 30, 2026 as set forth in the H.10 statistical release of the Federal Reserve Board. No representation is made that the RMB amounts could have been, or could be, converted, realized or settled into US$ at that rate on September 30, 2026, or at any other rate.

About Sunlands

Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG) (“Sunlands” or the “Company”), formerly known as Sunlands Online Education Group, is a leader in China’s adult online education market and China’s adult personal interest learning market. With a one to many live streaming platform, Sunlands offers various degree- or diploma-oriented post-secondary courses as well as professional certification preparation, professional skills and interest courses. Students can access the Company's services either through PC or mobile applications. The Company's online platform cultivates a personalized, interactive learning environment by featuring a virtual learning community and a vast library of educational content offerings that adapt to the learning habits of its students. Sunlands offers a unique approach to education research and development that organizes subject content into Learning Outcome Trees, the Company's proprietary knowledge management system. Sunlands has a deep understanding of the educational needs of its prospective students and offers solutions that help them achieve their goals.

About Non-GAAP Financial Measures

We use gross billings, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP operating cost and expenses, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP net income per share, each a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes.

We define gross billings for a specific period as the total amount of cash received for the sale of course packages, net of the total amount of refunds paid in such period. Our management uses gross billings as a performance measurement because we generally bill our students for the entire course tuition at the time of sale of our course packages and recognize revenue proportionally over a period. EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, and income tax expenses. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, income tax expenses and impairment loss on long-lived assets. We believe that gross billings, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA provide valuable insight into the sales of our course packages and the performance of our business.

These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, their most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. A reconciliation of the historical non-GAAP financial measures to their respective most directly comparable GAAP measure has been provided in the tables included below. Investors are encouraged to review the reconciliation of the historical non-GAAP financial measures to their respective most directly comparable GAAP financial measures. As gross billings, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, operating cost and expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, general and administrative expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, sales and marketing expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, product development expenses excluding share-based compensation expenses, income from operations excluding share-based compensation expenses, and basic and diluted net income per share excluding share-based compensation expenses have material limitations as an analytical metric and may not be calculated in the same manner by all companies, they may not be comparable to other similarly titled measures used by other companies. In light of the foregoing limitations, you should not consider gross billings, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA as a substitute for, or superior to, their respective most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. We encourage investors and others to review our financial information in its entirety and not rely on a single financial measure.

SHANGHAI, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ATRenew Inc. ("ATRenew" or the "Company") (NYSE: RERE), a pioneer in technology-driven recycling and trade-in solutions for consumer products in China, today announced its unaudited financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Total net revenues grew by 25.3% to RMB6,452.9 million (US$962.5 million) from RMB5,149.2 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Income from operations increased by 57.9% to RMB190.7 million (US$28.5 million) from RMB120.8 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP)1 grew by 50.7% to RMB211.5 million (US$31.5 million) from RMB140.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Net income increased by 53.6% to RMB139.5 million (US$20.8 million) from RMB90.8 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted net income (non-GAAP)1 grew by 45.3% to RMB160.1 million (US$23.9 million) from RMB110.2 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Number of consumer products transacted2 was 12.0 million compared to 10.9 million in the same period of 2025.

Mr. Kerry Xuefeng Chen, Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer of ATRenew, commented, "We are pleased to announce that ATRenew has once again delivered solid growth in the third quarter of 2026, with total net revenues reaching RMB6,452.9 million, up 25.3% year-over-year. We have continued to refine our supply chain capabilities for pre-owned mobile phones and digital products, leveraging our industry-leading collection and fulfillment infrastructure to aggregate quality supply. By adhering to rigorous standards for refurbishment and preparation, we continue to advance quality standards in the pre-owned sector, offering users high-value, high-quality products. On the platform side, we have continued to execute our strategy of extending services to a broader base of small and medium-sized merchants, while enhancing the user experience and expanding the range of scenarios for our multi-category recycling business." 

Mr. Rex Chen, Chief Financial Officer of ATRenew, added, "In the third quarter of 2026, ATRenew's profitability continued to improve, with income from operations rising 57.9% year-over-year to RMB190.7 million and adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP) rising 50.7% year-over-year to RMB211.5 million. We also saw a year-over-year improvement in fulfillment and sales and marketing spending efficiency—a positive outcome driven by our focus on refined operations and economies of scale. Furthermore, we have actively pursued share repurchases, totaling approximately US$6.6 million in the third quarter, bringing the cumulative value of repurchases for the first nine months of 2026 to approximately US$13.5 million. Moving forward, we remain committed to scaling our business and enhancing operational efficiency, while continuing to create long-term value for both our users and our shareholders."

[1] For all measures labeled as "non-GAAP" on this page and following pages, please see "Unaudited Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" for more information.

[2] "Number of consumer products transacted" represents the number of consumer products distributed to merchants and consumers through transactions on the Company's PJT Marketplace, Paipai Marketplace and other channels the Company operates in a given period, prior to returns and cancellations, excluding the number of consumer products collected through AHS Recycle; a single consumer product may be counted more than once according to the number of times it is transacted on PJT Marketplace, Paipai Marketplace and other channels the Company operates through the distribution process to end consumer.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

REVENUE

Total net revenues increased by 25.3% to RMB6,452.9 million (US$962.5 million) from RMB5,149.2 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Net product revenues increased by 27.0% to RMB6,004.2 million (US$895.6 million) from RMB4,726.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in the sales of pre-owned consumer electronics through the Company's online channels.
  • Net service revenues increased by 6.1% to RMB448.7 million (US$66.9 million), compared to RMB422.8 million in the same period of 2025. This increase was primarily due to an increase in the service revenue generated from multi-category recycling business and PJT Marketplace.

OPERATING COSTS AND EXPENSES

Operating costs and expenses were RMB6,263.5 million (US$934.2 million), compared to RMB5,033.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 24.4%.

  • Merchandise costs were RMB5,140.1 million (US$766.7 million), compared to RMB4,094.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 25.5%. The increase was primarily due to the growth in product sales.
  • Fulfillment expenses were RMB510.4 million (US$76.1 million), compared to RMB437.1 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 16.8%. The increase was primarily due to (i) an increase in personnel costs driven by the growth of the Company's business, and (ii) an increase in operating center related expenses as the Company conducted more recycling and transaction activities compared with the same period of 2025.
  • Selling and marketing expenses were RMB449.3 million (US$67.0 million), compared to RMB363.9 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 23.5%. The increase was primarily due to (i) an increase in commission expenses in relation to channel service fees, and (ii) an increase in advertising expense.
  • General and administrative expenses were RMB94.5 million (US$14.1 million), compared to RMB74.1 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 27.5%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel costs, sales tax and associated charges, and share-based compensation expenses.
  • Research and development expenses were RMB69.1 million (US$10.3 million), compared to RMB63.8 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 8.3%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel costs.

INCOME FROM OPERATIONS

Income from operations was RMB190.7 million (US$28.5 million), representing an increase of 57.9% from RMB120.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP) was RMB211.5 million (US$31.5 million), representing an increase of 50.7% from RMB140.3 million in the same period of 2025.

NET INCOME

Net income was RMB139.5 million (US$20.8 million), representing an increase of 53.6% from RMB90.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted net income (non-GAAP) was RMB160.1 million (US$23.9 million), representing an increase of 45.3% from RMB110.2 million in the same period of 2025.

BASIC AND DILUTED NET INCOME PER ORDINARY SHARE

Basic and diluted net income per ordinary share were RMB0.87 (US$0.13) and RMB0.87 (US$0.13), compared to RMB0.56 and RMB0.56 in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted basic and diluted net income per ordinary share (non-GAAP) were RMB1.00 (US$0.15) and RMB0.99 (US$0.15), compared to RMB0.68 and RMB0.68 in the same period of 2025.

CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS, RESTRICTED CASH, SHORT-TERM INVESTMENTS AND FUNDS RECEIVABLE FROM THIRD PARTY PAYMENT SERVICE PROVIDERS

Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments and funds receivable from third party payment service providers were RMB1,941.5 million (US$289.6 million) as of September 30, 2026, as compared to RMB2,187.4 million as of December 31, 2025.

Business Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company currently expects its total revenues to be between RMB7,780.0 million and RMB7,880.0 million, representing an increase of 24.4% to 26.0% year-over-year. This forecast only reflects the Company's current and preliminary views on the market and operational conditions, which are subject to change.

Recent Developments

Share Repurchase Update

On June 30, 2025, the board of directors of the Company (the "Board") authorized a new share repurchase program, under which the Company may repurchase up to US$50 million of its shares (including ADSs) over a 12-month period starting from June 30, 2025. On May 19, 2026, the Board authorized an extension of the existing share repurchase program for an additional 12-month period commencing from June 30, 2026, with other key terms remaining unchanged. During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased a total of approximately 1.6 million ADSs for approximately US$6.6 million. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cumulatively repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADSs for approximately US$21.4 million, with approximately US$28.6 million remaining available for repurchases under the share repurchase program.

Proposed Hong Kong Listing

The Company has previously submitted an application on a confidential basis for the listing of, and permission to deal in, its Class A ordinary shares on the Main Board of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited (the "Proposed Listing"). The Proposed Listing is intended to enhance the Company's access to Hong Kong's capital markets, broaden its investor base by reaching more institutional and retail investors in Asia, and raise its international profile.

The details of the Proposed Listing have not been finalized. The Proposed Listing remains subject to, among other things, approval by the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, completion of the filing with the China Securities Regulatory Commission, and the Company's final decision to proceed. There can be no assurance as to whether or when the Proposed Listing will take place. This disclosure is neither an offer to sell nor a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor shall there be any offer, solicitation or sale of the Company's securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation, or sale would be unlawful.

The Company remains committed to its previously announced shareholder return plan for fiscal years 2025 through 2027. Under the plan, the Company intends to return at least 60% of its annual adjusted net income to shareholders through share repurchases, cash dividends, or a combination of both. The timing, form and amount of these returns remain subject to the discretion of the Company's board of directors, taking into account the Company's financial performance, cash position, capital requirements and applicable laws and regulations.

About ATRenew Inc.

Headquartered in Shanghai, ATRenew Inc. is a pioneer in technology-driven recycling and trade-in solutions for consumer products in China. Since inception in 2011, ATRenew has been on a mission to give a second life to all idle goods, reducing the environmental impact of pre-owned consumer products by facilitating recycling, trade-ins and distribution that prolong their lifecycle. ATRenew's open platform integrates C2B, B2B, and B2C capabilities to empower its online and offline services. Powered by proprietary technologies and a scalable platform ecosystem, ATRenew enhances transaction efficiency and pricing transparency for consumers and merchants alike while advancing circular economy standards in China. ATRenew is a participant in the United Nations Global Compact, and adheres to its principles-based approach to responsible business.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company also uses certain non-GAAP financial measures in evaluating its business. For example, the Company uses adjusted income from operations, adjusted net income and adjusted net income per ordinary share as supplemental measures to review and assess its financial and operating performance. The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation, or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Adjusted income from operations is income from operations excluding the share-based compensation expenses and amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions. Adjusted net income is net income excluding the share-based compensation expenses and amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions and tax effects of amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions. Adjusted net income per ordinary share is adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by weighted average number of shares used in calculating net income per ordinary share.

The Company presents non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by the Company's management to evaluate the Company's financial and operating performance and formulate business plans. The Company believes that adjusted income from operations and adjusted net income help identify underlying trends in the Company's business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that are included in income from operations and net income. DISTRIBUTED-WORKFORCE/OAKLAND, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Square Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) are teaming up to make banking and payments simpler for Australian businesses and give them greater control over their cash flow.

For small businesses, including those in retail and hospitality, cash flow matters, margins matter and time matters. The partnership combines NAB’s business banking expertise with Square’s leading payments and business tools to make it easier for customers to manage the everyday work of running a business.

Initially, the partnership will provide eligible NAB customers using Square access to Square’s flexible transfer feature, giving them more control over when their available funds are sent to their NAB Business Transaction Account.

From February next year, businesses can set a close of day time for each day of the week, with Square initiating the transfer of their available funds to their NAB Business Transaction Account 15 minutes later.

NAB Group Executive Business and Private Banking Andrew Auerbach said the partnership reflected the bank’s ambition to keep supporting customers to make running their business easier.

“Many hospitality and retail businesses don’t operate nine to five,” Mr. Auerbach said.

“A restaurant might finish trading late at night and need to pay suppliers the next morning. A café might need to buy tomorrow’s produce, so their banking and payments need to work around how they do business.

“NAB already supports businesses of all shapes and sizes across Australia. We want to keep raising the bar by finding practical ways to make running them easier.

“These sound like small things, but they can make a big difference when you’re running a business. Flexible transfer is the first Square feature being made available through the partnership and we want to build on it.”

Block Global Partnerships Lead Morgan Kuntze said the partnership combined Square’s technology and understanding of sellers with NAB’s expertise in business banking.

“Square works with businesses every day, helping them take payments and manage the day-to-day work that sits behind making a sale,” Ms. Kuntze said.

“By partnering with NAB, we can connect that experience more closely with banking and find new ways to make managing money simpler for sellers.

“Flexible transfer is the first step. Sellers can set their close of day schedule around the way their business operates, and Square automatically initiates the transfer of their available funds.”

For Axil Coffee Roasters, which has grown from a single Hawthorn cafe to more than 16 locations and hundreds of wholesale partners, managing cash flow is part of the everyday reality of running a growing hospitality business.

“There’s no standard working day in hospitality,” said Axil Managing Director David Makin.

“Some of our venues open incredibly early, others trade later, and every day we’re managing staff, stock and suppliers across the business.

“Being able to set our transfer schedule around how we actually trade gives us another level of control over our cash flow.

“We need the flexibility. The more our banking and payments can fit around how the business actually operates, rather than the other way around, the better.”

Through the partnership, NAB and Square plan to build on flexible transfer by exploring further ways to connect banking and payments, simplify cash flow and make it easier for Australian businesses to operate and grow.

NAB has opened up the ability for businesses to express interest in the partnership ahead of the full launch in early 2027 - click here for more information.

Notes to editors:

  • NAB’s current standard settlement time is 9.30pm AEST daily.
  • Square’s flexible transfers require a linked and eligible NAB Business Transaction Account. The availability of funds in the linked bank account may be affected by NAB processing requirements.
  • Square applies transfer limits ranging from $5 to $50,000 AUD per day (new sellers are limited to $5,000 AUD per day until eligible for a higher limit). Flexible Transfers may not be available in limited circumstances beyond Square’s control, including where the linked bank account is not eligible for real-time payments or where there is downtime or delay affecting the New Payments Platform. Square’s Terms of Service apply.

About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighbourhood favourites. In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities. Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. For more information, visit squareup.com.

About NAB
At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. About 88% of the Group’s workforce are located in Australia and New Zealand, while others work in Asia, London, New York and Paris. NAB is proud to be Australia’s largest business lender. We stand by our customers, and they have our ongoing support.

DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jacobs (NYSE: J) has been selected by Sanofi as the Engineering, Procurement and Construction Management (EPCM) partner for a new insulin manufacturing facility in Frankfurt, Germany.

Located alongside Sanofi’s established insulin manufacturing campus, the facility will support the production of multiple insulin products and strengthen supply reliability.

Jacobs will provide integrated EPCM services spanning design, procurement, construction management and commissioning. Building on its involvement during early project development, Jacobs will leverage existing site infrastructure and advanced manufacturing technologies to deliver a state-of-the-art facility.

Jacobs Executive Vice President Sean Sommer said: "Our life sciences legacy began in 1943, when our founder, Dr. Joe Jacobs, was part of the team that enabled the first commercial-scale production of penicillin. More than 80 years later, we continue to deliver the advanced manufacturing facilities behind some of the world's most important therapies."

The project will incorporate advanced manufacturing systems that support efficient and reliable operations. Jacobs will deploy an integrated team spanning engineering, procurement, project controls, construction management, commissioning, quality and safety to deliver the project from design through startup.

This award further strengthens Jacobs' position as a leading solutions provider to global pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturers. Earlier this year, Engineering News-Record (ENR) ranked Jacobs the No. 1 Pharmaceuticals Design Firm, reflecting its leadership delivering advanced pharmaceutical manufacturing and biomanufacturing facilities. For example, Jacobs is providing EPCM services for FUJIFILM Biotechnologies' $3.2 billion Holly Springs campus, one of North America's largest biomanufacturing facilities, underscoring Jacobs' role in delivering complex life sciences investments at scale.

In Germany, Jacobs continues to deliver some of the country's most critical infrastructure and advanced manufacturing investments. Recent work includes SuedLink, one of the world's largest underground high-voltage power cable projects, a framework with TransnetBW supporting Germany's grid expansion and energy transition, and thyssenkrupp Steel's major industrial decarbonization program. With more than 300 employees across three offices in Germany, Jacobs provides integrated solutions spanning life sciences, energy, infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, helping drive innovation, resilience and long-term economic growth.

HONG KONG, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NetEase, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTES and HKEX: 9999, "NetEase" or the "Company"), a leading internet and game services provider, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues were RMB27.9 billion (US$4.2 billion), a decrease of 1.8% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
    • Games and related value-added services net revenues were RMB22.9 billion (US$3.4 billion), a decrease of 1.7% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
    • Youdao net revenues were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million), a decrease of 12.3% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
    • NetEase Cloud Music net revenues were RMB1.9 billion (US$290.3 million), a slight decrease of 0.9% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
    • Innovative businesses and others net revenues were RMB1.5 billion (US$229.7 million), an increase of 7.1% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB19.0 billion (US$2.8 billion), an increase of 4.8% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
  • Total operating expenses were RMB9.6 billion (US$1.4 billion), a decrease of 5.4% compared with the same quarter of 2025.
  • Net income attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB8.4 billion (US$1.3 billion). Non-GAAP net income attributable to the Company's shareholders was RMB9.2 billion (US$1.4 billion).[1]
  • Basic net income per share was US$0.39 (US$1.96 per ADS). Non-GAAP basic net income per share was US$0.43 (US$2.13 per ADS).[1]

[1] As used in this announcement, non-GAAP net income attributable to the Company's shareholders and non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per share and per ADS are defined to exclude share-based compensation expenses. See the unaudited reconciliation of GAAP and non-GAAP results at the end of this announcement.

Third Quarter 2026 and Recent Operational Highlights

  • Sustained engagement across established titles, underscoring the lasting appeal of our gaming portfolio. The Fantasy Westward Journey franchise, Identity V, Eggy Party, Sword of Justice and Where Winds Meet continued to captivate diverse player communities through content updates, gameplay innovation and crossover collaborations.
  • Strengthened our global appeal through differentiated gaming experiences and continued content innovation. Marvel Rivals deepened engagement with players worldwide through new features and fresh content, while Where Winds Meet surpassed 100 million players globally in August 2026, highlighting our growing capabilities in game development and live operations for the global market.
  • Advanced our diverse pipeline of games spanning more genres, gameplay experiences and themes. We progressed development and launch preparations for Ananta, which is currently scheduled for a multiplatform global launch on January 15, 2027. We also began rolling out player tests for several other titles in development.

"In the third quarter, we remained committed to delivering thoughtfully crafted game content and nurturing lasting player communities through fresh and compelling experiences," said Mr. William Ding, Chief Executive Officer and Director of NetEase. "While we continue to evolve our established titles with content and gameplay mechanics that appeal to a broader range of players, we are also steadily advancing our titles in development across genres, platforms and markets.

"Looking ahead, we remain focused on bringing together creative vision, technological innovation and strong execution to deliver games that stand the test of time. By continuing to strengthen our development and live operations capabilities, we aim to bring exceptional gaming experiences to vibrant player communities worldwide, creating long-term value for our partners and shareholders," Mr. Ding concluded.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net Revenues

Net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB27.9 billion (US$4.2 billion), compared with RMB30.1 billion and RMB28.4 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Net revenues from games and related value-added services were RMB22.9 billion (US$3.4 billion) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB25.0 billion and RMB23.3 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. Net revenues from the operation of online games accounted for approximately 97.5% of the segment's net revenues for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 97.7% and 97.6% for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The quarter-over-quarter decrease was primarily due to lower net revenues from certain self-developed games.

Net revenues from Youdao were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB1.5 billion and RMB1.6 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to decreased net revenues from its smart devices and online marketing services.

Net revenues from NetEase Cloud Music were RMB1.9 billion (US$290.3 million) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB2.0 billion each for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025.

Net revenues from innovative businesses and others were RMB1.5 billion (US$229.7 million) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB1.6 billion and RMB1.4 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB8.8 billion (US$1.3 billion), compared with RMB8.9 billion and RMB10.2 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The year-over-year decrease was mainly due to lower revenue-sharing costs.

Gross Profit

Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB19.0 billion (US$2.8 billion), compared with RMB21.2 billion and RMB18.2 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB9.6 billion (US$1.4 billion), compared with RMB9.1 billion and RMB10.2 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The quarter-over-quarter increase was primarily due to increased marketing expenses. The year-over-year decrease was primarily due to decreased marketing expenses and general and administrative expenses.

Other Income/(Expenses)

Other income/(expenses) consisted of investment income/(loss), interest income, net exchange gains/(losses) and others. The quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year fluctuations in other income/(expenses) were mainly due to fair value changes of listed equity securities.

Income Tax

The Company recorded a net income tax charge of RMB1.9 billion (US$275.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB2.5 billion and RMB1.3 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 17.8%, compared with 25.5% and 13.0% for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively. The effective tax rate represents certain estimates by the Company as to the tax obligations and benefits applicable to it in each quarter.

Net Income and Non-GAAP Net Income

Net income attributable to the Company's shareholders totaled RMB8.4 billion (US$1.3 billion) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB7.0 billion and RMB8.6 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Basic net income was US$0.39 per share (US$1.96 per ADS) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$0.33 per share (US$1.63 per ADS) and US$0.40 per share (US$2.01 per ADS) for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Non-GAAP net income attributable to the Company's shareholders totaled RMB9.2 billion (US$1.4 billion) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB7.7 billion and RMB9.5 billion for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

Non-GAAP basic net income was US$0.43 per share (US$2.13 per ADS) for the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$0.36 per share (US$1.80 per ADS) and US$0.44 per share (US$2.22 per ADS) for the preceding quarter and the same quarter of 2025, respectively.

  • Opening ceremony attended by Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation, Jack Chambers, TD; Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Peter Burke, TD; and Dexcom President and CEO Jake Leach.
  • Official opening marks next chapter for Dexcom’s investment in Ireland and manufacturing presence in Europe.
  • Since announcing plans to create 1,000 roles at its Athenry facility in 2024, Dexcom has filled almost 500 positions and will continue recruiting for the remaining roles as the site and production scale over the coming years.
  • Official opening, in the week following World Diabetes Day, celebrates the contributions of Dexcom Athenry staff to the CGM manufacturing process and impact on the lives of those living with diabetes.

 

ATHENRY, Ireland--(BUSINESS WIRE)--DexCom, Inc. (Nasdaq: DXCM), a global leader in continuous glucose monitoring, today officially opened its state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Athenry, County Galway, marking a major milestone in the company’s investment in Ireland and its manufacturing presence in Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The official opening ceremony, attended by Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation, Jack Chambers, TD; Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment, Peter Burke, TD; Dexcom President and CEO Jake Leach; and other senior Dexcom leaders, follows the start of commercial production at Athenry in October. The official opening celebrates Athenry’s transition from construction to commercial manufacturing and establishes the site as an important part of the company’s global manufacturing network.

Discussing Dexcom’s investment in the West of Ireland, An Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, TD, said: “The official opening of Dexcom’s Athenry facility is a tremendous vote of confidence in the people and talent of the West of Ireland. It is particularly encouraging to see almost 500 people already part of the team, building careers in a world-leading industry and contributing to technologies that make a real difference to people's lives. These are the kinds of high-quality employment opportunities that strengthen communities, attract further investment and help ensure that Galway and the wider region continue to thrive. The opening of this facility is an important milestone, not only for Dexcom, but for Athenry and Ireland's continued success as a global centre for medical technology.”

Dexcom first broke ground on the Athenry facility in January 2024, announcing plans to create more than 1,000 jobs and invest approximately €300 million over five years. Today, the site has assembled a team of almost 500 people, the vast majority from the West of Ireland. The remaining roles are expected to be advertised and filled in the coming years as production at the site scales to support demand for CGM across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the rest of the world.

Jake Leach, President and Chief Executive Officer of Dexcom, said: “The opening of Athenry is an important milestone for Dexcom, establishing our first manufacturing presence in EMEA and reinforcing our long-term commitment to Ireland. As we bring Dexcom CGM to more people around the world, expanding our manufacturing capabilities is fundamental to supporting the continued growth of our business. With large-scale manufacturing facilities now operating across the U.S., Europe, and Asia Pacific, we are well positioned to support our ambitious growth plans, and Athenry will play a critical role in the next chapter of Dexcom's global story.”

Supported by the Irish Government through IDA Ireland, Dexcom’s Athenry facility strengthens the West of Ireland’s medtech cluster, which employs 16,000 people across Galway, Mayo and Roscommon.

The official opening of Dexcom Athenry takes place in the week following World Diabetes Day, observed Nov. 14. The opening date was chosen to recognise the diabetes community and celebrate the impact of Dexcom employees on the development and manufacturing of CGM technology. The diabetes community was represented at the opening by Diabetes Ireland, International Diabetes Federation Europe and Thriveabetes. Norah Casey, an Irish businesswoman and entrepreneur, also spoke at the event, sharing “A Letter to Diabetes,” a personal reflection on her life with diabetes.

Columba McGarvey, Senior Vice President, Global Manufacturing Operations at Dexcom, said: “What makes Dexcom Athenry special is its people. We have already assembled a remarkable team of almost 500 people, the vast majority from right here in the West of Ireland, and together they are now making CGM sensors that can help transform how millions of people worldwide manage their health. Behind every sensor we make is a person living with diabetes, and the knowledge that our work can help make their lives easier, healthier and more fulfilling is what makes our team’s contribution so meaningful.”

Notes to Editors

Dexcom currently employs almost 500 people at Athenry and continues to recruit additional employees across a range of disciplines. Further information on opportunities at Dexcom Athenry is available at careers.dexcom.com.

About DexCom, Inc.

Dexcom empowers people to take control of health through innovative biosensing technology. Founded in 1999, Dexcom has pioneered and set the standard in glucose biosensing for more than 25 years. Its technology has transformed how people manage diabetes and track their glucose, helping them feel more in control and live more confidently.
